usefulnessAfterMissProposal.rationale: Separate inaccessible service from disclosure, modification and attribution. Feedback does not teach choosing RTO, RPO or recovery architecture.
Identify inaccurate changed records even when the actor has access permission; accessible but incorrect data is the integrity cue.
Feedback qualifies that credential and occupancy controls accompany interlocking; authentication or two doors alone does not guarantee single-person entry.
Distinguish splitting sensitive duties from limiting each actor’s permissions, rotating jobs or requiring time off. The stated protection reduces unilateral abuse only.
Feedback separates independent deployment approval from permission minimization and control layering; it expressly avoids guaranteeing malicious-code detection.

Feedback says a digest needs a trusted basis: replaceable message and digest do not establish integrity. Authentication-code/signature vocabulary is teaching context, not separate assessed competence.
The correction contrasts divided approver/executor responsibilities with one person’s permission scope and role changes over time.
Feedback distinguishes joint participation from splitting a secret and warns that neither automatically prevents collusion. The compound stem warrants scope review rather than two outcomes.
Feedback contrasts target deception with execution isolation and data-movement controls; decoy interactions require context and isolation from production.
The feedback identifies change rather than loss of access, disclosure or denial of action; permission and attribution remedies are unassessed teaching suggestions.
The correction focuses on one actor’s minimum necessary resources, distinct from splitting a transaction between actors or layering protections.
Feedback separates the enclosed interlocked passage from a turnstile, presence sensor and vehicle barrier. Keep the qualification that door sequencing alone does not ensure one-person admission.
